By night, it transforms into a cozy table lamp that casts soft light. A porcelain-style pot adds another dimension of realism to the design, and battery power makes it portable and easy to operate.

These charming duck toilet bolt covers will bring a smile to your face every time you enter the bathroom —and just wait until your house guests spot them. Offered as a set of two, the sleek ceramic covers slide right on exposed screws. One shopper gushed, “They’re adorbs, actually ceramic, inexpensive, require zero installation skills, and spruce up the ol’ toidy perfectly. [...] My only regret is not having discovered them sooner.”

If you find it easier to focus while keeping your hands occupied, then these fidget toys are exactly what you need. Each of the included four sensory toys has a different color and soothing texture for stress relief and improved concentration. Simply twist and flip the sides for a satisfying sensory sensation that’s quiet and discreet.

Creating custom labels and stickers is fun and easy with this Bluetooth mini printer. It uses thermal printing technology to expertly print graphics, photos, and more — all effortlessly customizable in the free app. And since it’s not much larger than the average cell phone, you can take it along with you wherever you go.

This aesthetic stationery set has everything you might want or need to take notes or journal. It comes with a colorful assortment of pastel mechanical pencils, erasers, lead refills, and even a carrying case for convenient storage and portability.

Why dirty more dishes than necessary when you can cook your entire meal in one pan? Like this absolutely genius divided grill pan with three separate sections. It's crafted from aluminum and features a nonstick granite coating, which means it’s durable and easy to wipe clean. Compatible with all stovetops, this is a cookware MVP.

Keep all your tech in like-new condition with this must-have keyboard cleaning kit. A variety of precision tools, sponges, and brushes won’t shed or scratch, and they promise to make it easy and safe to clean everything from laptops to earbuds. Plus, everything fits neatly into the carrying case for convenient storage and portability. With a 4.6-star rating after 6,000+ reviews, it’s a cleaning set that will get the job done.

Melt away stress and anxiety with this tin of ferrite stones. The naturally magnetic stones cling together like puddy, providing a malleable mass that not only feels good to the touch but also produces a calming sound when rubbed together. They’re especially great for meditating and sensory play, or just for getting kids (or yourself) off screens.

This is about to become your new favorite blanket that you’ll be reaching for all year round. Yup, it’s that good. Not only is the ribbed fleece ultra plush and cozy, but it’s lightweight and breathable too, offering just the right amount of warmth. And it’s available in a ton of colors and sizes so you can get one for your bed, the couch, and beyond for easy, luxurious texture. Choose from nearly three dozen colors and in all the sizes you could want.

This brilliant kitchen gadget is perfect for saving space. That’s because it contains six kitchen tools in one portable and easy-to-store keychain design. Tools include a cheese grater, ginger grinder, pizza cutter wheel, bottle opener, vegetable and fruit peeler, and an herb stripper. It’s ideal for small spaces, camping trips, or dorm dwellers.

There’s something so satisfying about seeing your pics print instantly — and this camera lets you experience that right out of the box, since it comes with three rolls of printing paper. In addition to the 32GB memory card and USB charging cable, it also comes with markers to add fun doodles. With 16x zoom and even a timer shoot option, this little camera packs a lot of functionality into its compact size.

This amazing multi-purpose wallet holds it all — from credit cards and cash to passports and even your phone. And it even helps protect from digital theft with the built-in RFID blocking shield. The textured faux leather outer gives it an expensive look and feel but it’s actually really affordable. Choose from tons of colors to suit your vibe.

These innovative shoelaces first premiered on Shark Tank and promise to “turn every shoe into a slip on.” They’re made from super stretchy elastic for the ultimate comfort and flexibility. And since they feature a lightly textured surface, they stay put once tied, making them perfect for kids and adults. They’re available in a range of sizes and colors, so you can outfit the whole family.

Car cup holders are great but what about a holder that can hold an entire meal (plus your phone)? That’s exactly what this amazing car tray table does. The base fits right into a car cup holder and offers a generously sized tray on a rotating arm that’s adjustable. And it even has a built-in cell phone holder.

Simple to put in place, this bathtub filter can clean up to 2,500 gallons of water for plenty of baths. It features eight layers of filtration materials, including activated carbon, zeolite, calcium sulfite, and more. One fan wrote, “It really works as well, my skin is not dry when I get out.Easy to use, doesn’t impede water flow to any noticeable degree.”

Judging by the portable size, you’d never guess that this clever roll-up jewelry organizer contains three roomy tiers — each lined with a soft, suede-like material to protect your valuables. When closed, it looks just like a leather clutch, complete with embossed detail, a convenient snap closure, and a cute tassel. No wonder it has a 4.7-star rating after nearly 5,000 reviews.

Literally block out the noise with these innovative earplugs. Silicone tips help block up to 17 decibels of noise, providing instant protection and relief. And the loop design, complete with a gold-tone finish, helps them pass for a fashion accessory, which means you can enjoy peace and quiet without sacrificing style.

With an ingenious, space-saving design, it’s no wonder this two-in-one whisk has earned a near-perfect, 4.7-star rating after more than 5,000 shopper have weighed in. Open it into a balloon shape for perfectly whipped cream or collapse it flat to create luscious sauces (and to save space in your kitchen drawers). Plus, the wires are made from silicone-coated stainless steel for maximum durability with no-scratch benefits.

Forget breaking your back or risking a slip and fall in the shower when you can get this clever foot scrubber mat instead. Step onto the soft silicone bristles to treat yourself to a luxurious, exfoliating foot scrub with included acupressure points. Strong suction cups keep it securely in place.

This cuddly little panda lamp makes for the perfect night-light or reading light. It features dimming capabilities for bright and low light options, and a timer means you can set it and fall asleep knowing it will turn off on its own. Since it’s rechargeable via USB, it’s so easy to toss in a suitcase for light on the go.

Boost the storage and organization in your car — and add some style — with this car center console cover. It has two slots to hold your phone, wallet, and more. With quilted faux leather and sparkly gems lining the sides, it’s as nice-looking as it is functional.

Whether you’re birdwatching, traveling, or watching a game or concert from far away, this powerful monocular telescope delivers bright, high-contrast images across a wide field of view. It features 16x magnification with a large 52mm objective lens, letting you zoom in on sights without lugging around bulky gear. Waterproof and fog-resistant, it’s a dependable little tool for outdoor use.

Use this portable outdoor fire pit for dinner parties, backyard hangouts, and more. It’s made from stainless steel and features an easy-to-light design that won’t produce smoke. You can use both pellets or wood for the coziest-ever atmosphere.

This three-in-one bedtime companion offers so much functionality. Not only is it an handy digital alarm clock, but it also offers 10 ambient lighting options and seven soothing sounds. Choose from three cute colors within the listing to suit your bedroom decor.

This manual food chopper is perfect for meal prep at home or on the go. It features three sharp stainless steel blades that can chop everything from fruit to veggies, and it even separates and whisks eggs. Just turn the smooth handle to operate. Remove the blade and insert the basket to turn it into a salad spinner.

Ideal for use with steamers or small irons, this glove is easy to loop onto your hand. Once you do, the thick sponge material will protect your appendage from the heat of the steamer or iron — it essentially turns your hand into a small ironing board. One reviewer wrote, “I ordered this to use with a new portable steamer. It made steaming garments so much safer and easier. No more worries about burning fingers while holding the garments to steam. Great idea and great product.”

Shoppers are raving about Owala’s FreeSip tumbler, which boasts a 4.7-star overall rating after more than 100,000 reviews. Designed with both a built-in straw and a sipping hole, it’s totally leakproof — just press the button to drink. Plus, the double-wall stainless steel construction keeps hot drinks at just the right temperature for up to six hours. Choose from dozens of fun colors.

Turn your smartphone or tablet into a high-tech gadget with the help of this endoscope camera. It has a tk long cord, and on the end there’s a flashlight and you can attach a mirror, magnet, or hook. One reviewer wrote, “This is awesome!! Can use it anywhere and my kids enjoy using it as well. Multifunctional! Fun to use! Very helpful for finding things and issues with things.”

The coolest way to put your hair up, this set comes with two metal hair pins that look like giant safety pins. Ach one is 5 inches long. “Way better quality than I thought. [...] I haven’t experienced any snagging! [...] one I can use for also accessorizing like on necklaces or purses too because it’s SO CUTE,” wrote one shopper.

With three silver-toned shelves in a set, you’ll be able to display all your books in such an elegant way. Reviewers report that installation is easy, with all hardware included. Each shelf can hold up to 20 pounds, so they’re guaranteed to hold up to your growing collection.

These screwdrivers come in a set of six, and each one is a different size and orientation for different uses. The heads are magnetic, too, so you don’t have to worry about them clinging to your screws.

Whether you want to give this sticker maker to your kids for craft time or use it yourself for labeling everything in the pantry, it’ll be beyond useful. It connects via Bluetooth to an app so you can truly make whatever your heart desires. It uses thermal technology to create the labels and comes with a roll of sticker paper to get you started.

This programmable outlet adapter comes with a remote so you can control everything from your lights, TV, and more without ever having to get up (and from up to 100 feet away). Just plug them right into your existing outlets, plug in a lamp (or TV or anything, really), and sync them to the remote to begin using them right away.

Protect your counter from scratches and heat (like from a flat iron or curling iron) by putting down this nonslip silicone mat. It can withstand up to 464 degrees Fahrenheit and measures 15.7 by 11.8 inches to holds plenty of things.

If putting things in their proper place soothes you, check out this mini bookshelf. It latches shut to look like a piece of decor but can be shaken (while closed) or dumped out, allowing you to place the 185 tiny booksback in place. This can keep your hands busy, clear your mind, and give you a little screen-free time to yourself.

Not only does this innovative spray bottle pump out mist so fine that you’d think it was powered by aerosol, but it does that without tiring out your hands. Simply press the feather-light trigger to release a continuous mist — even when held sideways or upside down. It’s perfect for hairstyling, plant care, and more.

Ditch that old phone stand that never seems to grip your phone right for this magnetic version that will literally never let you (aka your phone) down. This phone stand is slim and portable and features an adjustable and sturdy base. But the best part is the strong magnetic design. Just snap your phone on and get on with your business. Choose from more than a dozen colors to suit your space.

Whimsical yet useful, this cloud-shaped light mounts on the wall and has a simple pull chain for operation. It’s entirely cordless (and battery powered), allowing you to install it wherever you’d like — and it comes with everything you need to put it in place.

Whether you’re working with wood, paper, ceramic, or a different material, reach for these quick-drying acrylic paint pens. They have a different tip on either end for versaility, (fine tip and paint brush), and the ink dries with an eye-catching metallic finish.

If you’re still trying to touch up your makeup using your car’s sun visor mirror, do yourself a favor and upgrade to this portable vanity mirror. It fits right in your pocket but offers big convenience in the form of two mirrors (in 1X and 3X magnification) and bright lights along the borders. Clearly, it’s a best-selling beauty mirror for good reason.

“Works great! Easy to use and strong. Nice to have a rechargeable one. It has different power levels and handy light too. Perfect for keyboards and gaming consoles,” one shopper raved about this compressed air duster. Unlike a lot of others, it features five attachments and three speeds so you can use it to clean everything from laptops to cars.

Made of silicone for flexibility, these flexible headbands feature a metal core that maintains shape after you get them just right. “The silicone is so soft and thick. Comfortable and does not break my hair when taking off. I can wear it all day and don't realize I am wearing it. No more headaches. It easily slides off. Was at my hairdresser and she couldn't believe how great it gripped my hair and how it slid off so easily,” wrote one fan. The deep teeth of the combs help them stay put, as do little nubs on the inside.

Instead of leaving your sponge on the countertop, give it a permanent place to live with this bendable holder. You can loop it around the base of your faucet or bend it over the divider of a double sink. The perforated design helps your sponge dry quickly, while the open bottom means you can also use this for storing handled scrub brushes.

Building blocks have come a long way since most of us were kids, and this plant lovers set is the proof. Once assembled, you’ll be staring back at an amazing botanical scene. This tiny plants LEGO set is so cute that you’ll want to show it off to friends and family. With 758 pieces in a set, you’ll be building for hours.

Magnetic to stick to your vehicle, golf cart, or any metal surface around your home, this light is easily recharged via USB-C. Choose from various lighting modes: single flash, double flash, triple flash, penta flash, double-quadra flash, SOS, and white light mode. One reviewer wrote, “Very bright light. Almost blinding. Definitely visible at night from long distances. Perfect for putting on your car if you have to pull over on the side of the road. Everyone will see you from a mile away. Light works perfectly every time.”

Turn almost any bottle into a night-light with this clever bottle stopper that doubles as a lamp. Simply insert the rubber-lined stopper to create an air-tight seal, then tap the top to adjust the color temperature and brightness. It conveniently charges via USB cable, making it easy to keep powered.

Now you can toss all those smelly, sweaty caps right into the washer when you use these hat cages. The washer-ready cage creates a protective layer around most-sized caps, helping them keep their shape while getting nice and clean. Just place a cap between the cage, clip it closed, and toss it in the wash.

Water and your favorite coffee grinds are all that’s needed to make the perfect cup of joe when you use this ingenious portable coffee press. It’s easy to use and features a fine filter that ensures no bitterness or grit. And since it's compact and made from shatterproof Tritan, it’s ideal for taking on the go. One satisfied shopper gushed, “The AeroPress is absolutely worth the hype, especially if you’re picky and want one of the best (if not THE best) tasting brew you can make.”

Turn any toilet into a bidet with this best-selling handheld sprayer kit. It’s quick and easy to install and clips right to the toilet tank for easy access (or mount it to the wall). Plus, it features an adjustable water pressure sprayer and a flexible braided stainless steel hose for added convenience and durability.

Resembling the moon with its minimalist build, this alarm clock will look stunning on your nightstand — but it does so much more than. With gentle wake-up lighting, 10 soothing nature sounds, and a night-light function, it will create a serene oasis. It has three adjustable brightness levels, a snooze function, and multiple atmospheric lighting options, too.

Make the most of unused space in your car with this stick-on seat organizer. Made from high-quality PU leather, it’s soft yet durable, with neat stitching and a waterproof, scratch-resistant finish. Mount it to seat seams or flat surfaces to store your phone, cards, glasses, receipts, or other small essentials. It’s an affordable and space-saving addition to any ride.

Made of pink Himalayan salt, this two-pound rock is designed to hang from your showerhead or tub’s tap. As water flows over it, it adds minerals to your water for a spa-like experience. It even comes with a mesh bag for hanging dry between uses. You can also soak it in the tub as desired.

This squishy fidget toy has a soft, slow-rising texture that’s genuinely satisfying to squeeze. Use it to help clear and calm your mind through simple, repetitive motion. The elasticity makes it ideal for kneading during work, study, or downtime, offering a calming sensory outlet without screens or noise — and the butter scent is a fun bonus.

An elevated version of your usual fridge magnets, this pack of eight looks like detailed leaves for a fresh and lively look. Four styles come included and they measure nearly 2 inches long. One shopper wrote, “These were a very pleasant surprise. The magnet on them, for its small size, is VERY strong. [...] These look so much better than the myriad of souvenir magnet I have collected over the years. The colors and detail are really life like, not cheap looking.”

Designed for convenience, the mini torpedo level features strong magnets for hands-free use and LED-lit bubble vials that are easy to read in dim workspaces. It’s small enough to slip into a pocket or toolbox, and perfect for hanging pictures, aligning shelves, home renovation tasks, or DIY decorating. It’s a significant upgrade on traditional levels for a great price.

This roomy cat-shaped makeup bag keeps your everyday essentials contained without hogging counter space. The drawstring design opens wide so you can actually see what you packed, then cinches closed to keep your contents secure. Made from durable polyester with a playful 3D cat face, it’s a cheap, practical, and playful addition to your vanity, gym bag, or suitcase.

You can place your plant clippings in this four-vase propagation station and watch them thrive, even in low-light settings. That’s thanks to the integrated LED light strip that offers nine brightness settings. The durable beechwood design comes with an included USB port and charging cable to keep them juiced.

When your accessories should be just as fun as the outfit, reach for these LED scrunchies. They feature three light modes that glow, flash, or shine steadily, turning a simple ponytail or bun into a full-on statement. Soft yarn construction keeps them comfortable and breathable, while a woven texture helps the lights shine brighter for extra visual impact. Each set includes six scrunchies.

Life feeling like a dumpster fire? At least your writing utensils can match the mood when you have these ballpoint pens. Each one is topped with a mini dumpster fire with the message “I’m fine, it’s fine, everything is fine.” (Accurate.) And since 12 come in a pack, you can gift them to your coworkers, too.

This night-light is more like a tiny, illuminated work of art. Featuring a vintage-inspired stained glass globe, it casts a colorful glow on the wall behind it. The stepless dimmer on the side lets you get bright light or soft, cozy illumination that’s perfect for midnight snack runs to the kitchen.

These toe separators create plenty of space to help you get a neat, smudge-free pedicure. But let’s not bury the lede — the, colorful flowery shapes give them the most whimsical look (you might just find yourself swapping shades midweek to use them again). Another bonus use? They can help stretch out your toes and alleviate discomfort after a day spent in tight shoes.

Got an old piece of furniture you’re tired of looking at? Swap in these crystal knobs to breathe new life into it. They have a gorgeous, gem-like design wrapped in copper wire, totally transforming even your most basic IKEA dresser. Choose from several shades including sapphire blue and emerald green.

If your outdoor space is feeling lackluster in the evenings, it might be missing these solar-powered globe lights that create an instant cozy glow. The cracked glass surface feels vintage and magical, while the waterproof, weather-resistant design means you can leave them out even when the forecast calls for a downpour. Use them to line a walkway, to illuminate your patio table, or just scatter them around your garden.

Headrest hooks like these are an amazing way to keep purses and takeout bags up and off the floor (and not rolling around with every turn). This set takes things up a notch thanks to the pearl-dotted design that gives your interior some Chanel-inspired vibes. And though they look delicate, they can hold a hefty 44 pounds each.

Keeping your phone powered up in the car has never been easier... or more magical. This charger casts a starry projection on your car’s ceiling for a cool, galactic effect that you can turn off as needed. As for charging, you’ll get retractable Lightning and USB-C cables as well as two additional ports, making it easy to keep your devices juiced and ready to go.

The genius design of this laundry bag allows you to compress dirty clothing towards the end of a trip, freeing up precious space in your luggage for souvenirs. It has a handle at the top for toting around, and a one-way valve on the bottom or squeezing out excess air as you compress — no vaccum required. The inside is waterproof for damp items and keeps smells locked within.

This tiny garden gnome is living his best life on his swing perch — and the adorable figurine comes with twine for you to hang it wherever it will deliver the most joy. Crafted from durable, weatherproof resin, it’s a piece of yard decor that will hold up season after season.

Fresh flowers are a vibe but they can fade and wilt fast. That’s where this tiny copper charm comes in handy. Drop it in and it helps keep water free of slime and ensures your flowers last longer. “It’s not only so beautiful, but it miraculously works! [...] I usually get 1 week at best with plant food. With [this charm] I got 3 weeks,” raved one fan. It comes with a small pouch for storage.

Enjoy a serene aquarium vibe without the commitment of an aquarium: This special lamp is filled with jellyfish that float and dance through the water (thanks to the small motor inside). It plugs in for power, and there’s a handy timer function.

Not only are these tea bag bookmarks cute and colorful, but they also offer a clever option for keeping your spot in your current read. The bag will secure in between the pages, and the string will hang out the top for spotting. Six come in a pack.

Break up a stressful workday by playing in this miniature turtle sandbox ... it’s surprisingly calming. Included are small accessories (like shovels and buckets) for even more fun. And the shell keeps it closed when not in use.

This power failure alarm will beep when a power outage is detected on an item like your fridge, sump pump, furnace, etc. It’s a must-have. The alarm can be set to five volume levels and seven sirens, ensuring you can always hear it.

Run one of these therapy brushes along your skin for a soothing massage. Each one (three come with) features tons of soft bristles to help, and the portable size means you can toss it in your bag.

This charming bird candle is made entirely from real paraffin wax, yet the flickering “flame” is completely fake. It’s battery powered so there’s no hazard involved. Display it proudly on your mantle, tablescape, and more.

At-home pedicures are way easier to pull off with this foot rest that can be set to six different heights for adequate positioning. It’s nonslip, heavy duty (supporting up to 220 pounds), and folds flat for convenient storage.

Effortlessly peel garlic with this clever three-pack of garlic skin removers. The textured inner surface gently grips garlic skin, peeling it away with each rolling motion. As one shopper explained, “Peeling garlic can be tedious. This little gadget is amazing. Clove is inserted into the peeler, a few rolls back and forth (I use the palm of my hand) and out comes a perfectly peeled clove of garlic. Best thing you didn’t know you needed.”

This vintage yet modern table lamp is entirely cordless, so you can move it with you from table to nightstand to desk, and back again. The rechargeable design has an incredibly long batter life, providing up to 13 days of light. With three color temperatures to choose from, it makes any room feel more elegant.

These brass birds sit neatly on door hinge pins or attach to metal surfaces using discreet built-in magnets, adding a charming touch in unexpected places. Lightweight and easy to reposition, they can be placed on hinges, cabinets, shelves, picture frames, or any magnetic spot where you want a subtle upgrade. They’re the kind of decorative touch that shows your attention to detail. Each set comes with three birds.

#8048. Eight Sleep’s Alexandra Zatarain on women-centered tech, the science of better sleep, and planning a career around motherhood

By Sara Goldstein Updated Nov. 12, 2026

This article is sponsored by Eight Sleep. Thank you for supporting the brands that support Motherly and mamas.

Alexandra Zatarain helped build Eight Sleep into a tech unicorn, and she’s expecting her first child in January. Going through pregnancy while running a global company has reshaped how she sees her own body, her industry and the product she’s building. On this episode of The Motherly Podcast, the co-founder of the sleep-technology company talks about the research that showed Eight Sleep’s technology was improving men’s sleep more than women’s and what the company did about it, why sleep is the most important thing women can protect, and the career advice she wishes more women heard before becoming mothers.

Meet the expert: Alexandra Zatarain is the co-founder and VP of brand and marketing at Eight Sleep, the sleep-technology company behind the Pod. The Pod is an intelligent mattress cover that cools or heats each side to your ideal temperature automatically, maximizing deep sleep and minimizing wake-ups. A marketer and brand builder, she grew Eight Sleep from launch into a tech unicorn and helped create what the company calls the sleep fitness movement. Eight Sleep now sells in 37 countries. She’s expecting her first child in January with her husband, Matteo, the company’s co-founder and CEO.

Alexandra Zatarain: So many things. I just turned 37, and I’ve seen so many friends go through pregnancy before me. After my first trimester, I felt so bad, thinking, what a terrible friend I was. When you haven’t experienced it, you have such little empathy for what a woman’s body is going through, especially when life keeps demanding so much of you and it doesn’t stop. I really didn’t understand that you could feel so different in your body for so long. It’s built so much more admiration for women and what we go through, and it’s let me embrace a feminine side of myself that in tech you usually don’t get to bring out.

Alexandra Zatarain: It’s made me realize that the only way the world out there is going to change for our benefit as women and mothers is if more of us are the ones making the decisions. I just don’t see any way around it. We have a lot of parents at Eight Sleep, every executive on our team is a parent, but as a woman the experience is completely different. Unless we can share that first-hand knowledge, it’s going to be hard to make progress as fast as we need to. It’s unfortunate that it takes the first-person experience to become that advocate, because everyone should appreciate what mothers go through, given that we all come from a mother.

Alexandra Zatarain: A couple of years ago, our clinical team, which is more than 90% women, was analyzing data from our user base and noticed our technology had been improving men’s sleep more than women’s. They asked, what are we missing in how we design this? It turned out the algorithms that manage temperature while you sleep had been fed more data representing men than women. That’s a classic problem in science, where women are underrepresented because our bodies are more complex. You have to account for where someone is in their hormonal journey, pregnancy, postpartum, perimenopause. So we invested a couple million dollars into research and developed features from it. That changed how we think about ourselves, less about helping everyone in a broad way and more about solving specific problems women have had for ages.

Alexandra Zatarain: Sleep is the most important pillar of health. You would die sooner from sleep deprivation than from food deprivation, which tells you how fundamental it is. For women it matters even more because our hormones rule our lives, and sleep is the one tool we have to regulate them. If you sleep well, your chances of better hormonal balance go up significantly. It’s the best medicine we have, more than working out, more than any meal. The challenge is that those same hormones are often playing against us, making it harder to sleep well in different seasons of life, so keeping our routines as stable as possible helps counter what our bodies are going through.

Alexandra Zatarain: The mindset piece is really important. There’s so much going on, the anxiety, the intrusive thoughts, so not being too hard on yourself is the first step. Understanding that the season will pass should put you a little more at ease, because it’s not going to be your life forever. The other piece is setting yourself up with the right systems, and the most important one is available to everyone for free, which is routine. It helps your body a lot. When you do need to sleep, it’ll be easier for your body to fall asleep because it’s used to the schedule.

Alexandra Zatarain: I’m very rigid about my sleep schedule. I travel a lot, so sleep is number one for me. I make space for eight to nine hours every night, and I’m pretty good at hitting it. I go to bed by 9:30 or 10 every single night no matter where I am in the world, and I don’t really use an alarm unless I have to wake up before 6, because my body just wakes up on its own. That schedule is the thing that’s changed my life the most. Second to that is the environment, the temperature in my room and my bed, the lights going dark, no noise.

Alexandra Zatarain: I think of myself as an athlete, and we’re all sort of athletes in a way. My sport is making decisions about how to build this business, and that means I have to train, stay healthy and think long term. It’s not a sprint. We’ve been doing this for 12 years, so the question is how do I not burn out and stay here 20 or 30 years more. I’m also lucky I built this with my husband, so there’s no real line between business and personal life for us. It’s all mixed in, but it’s so purpose-driven that achieving that purpose every day is what feeds the energy.

Alexandra Zatarain: I’m very open with them about how intentional I was. I did my embryo freezing in my early 30s because of where I was in life. And I tell them that if they want a career after they have a family, the best time to build equity in that career is to push as hard as you can before. Know what you want, because time isn’t always on our side as women. Move up the ranks, so that by the time you have kids you have more flexibility and maybe a higher income. It is possible, but it takes planning, it will require compromises, and very importantly it will require the right partner.

Alexandra Zatarain: It starts with the people around you understanding what you truly need. Sometimes it’s as simple as the encouragement of, yes, go take a nap, yes, your body’s going through a lot. It gets harder once the baby’s home and the mom is maybe exclusively breastfeeding, because it really all falls on you. So have a plan in place ahead of time for how the load is going to be shared. Our partners are much more involved than previous generations, so have those conversations early. It doesn’t end with the birth plan. That’s where everything starts.

Alexandra Zatarain: The first trimester was difficult, a lot of nausea, and it was very hard to function at the level I’m used to. I almost never get sick, so feeling sick every day was a huge shift. It put me in the trajectory to build the team that would make it possible for me to become a mother, to figure out what to delegate and who to elevate, and I’ve built a stronger team as a result. But the biggest thing is that it’s taught me to let go. I can’t control how I feel every day. As a Type A person I always want to be in control, and this has been like therapy, learning that I’m not in control of my body. I’m building a human, and it’s fine if for this season things just work differently.

#8047. Neakasa Riko Fresh-Made Wet Meal Feeder Review 2026: Our Expert’s Opinion

Catster is reader-supported. When you buy via links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission at no cost to you. Learn more.

This review was created in partnership with Neakasa, who compensated us for our time and editorial work. However, our opinions and ratings remain entirely our ownâwe only recommend products we genuinely believe in, and all assessments reflect our honest experience and testing.

We give the Neakasa Riko Fresh-Made Wet Meal Feeder a rating of 4.8 out of 5 stars.

Youâve probably heard by now that feeding wet food to your cat is better than feeding dry food. This has a lot to do with hydration and moisture levels. As it turns out, most cats donât drink enough water, and a diet of dry food compounds the issue by further dehydrating them.

Feeding canned or wet food is a great solution to this issue. Unless, of course, you travel, work long hours, or otherwise donât have the bandwidth to open can after can for your hungry feline.

This is where the Neakasa Riko Fresh-Made Wet Meal Feeder comes in. This isnât another automatic wet cat food feeder that requires constant refilling and cleaning. Oh no, this is something completely new.

This revolutionary device fresh-grinds freeze-dried cat food, rehydrates it with filtered water, then serves it automaticallyâup to 20 meals per day! Never before has keeping your cat hydrated been so easy or so tasty.

But does this high-tech contraption live up to the hype? I had the opportunity to test this space-age automatic cat feeder with the help of my hungry-hippo kitty, Makoa. Keep reading to see what we liked about it and if itâs worth the purchase in my full Neakasa Riko Fresh-Made Wet Meal Feeder review.

Domestic cats are descended from African desert wild cats. These wild felines got most of their hydration from their prey. Their kidneys became ultra-efficient at retaining moisture, and their drive to find fresh water sources nearly disappeared completely.

Our house cats retain this same physiology and lack of interest in hunting down fresh water. The problem? They arenât typically chowing down on juicy rodents a dozen times a day. Which means they often donât get the moisture they need to keep those specialized kidneys healthy.

This is why 40% of cats over 10 years old and 80% of cats over 15 years old develop chronic kidney disease. After a lifetime of chronic dehydration, their kidneys simply canât keep up.

One solution is to increase the amount of water cats consume through their food by offering wet food or adding water to their dry food. This is doable if you are home during meal times every day. But if you work long hours, have a million other things to juggle, or occasionally (or often) travel, feeding moist meals consistently becomes more of a challenge.

Some turn to automatic wet food feeders that keep pre-prepared portions of wet food cool, automatically opening each portion on a set schedule. While these work in the short term, they hold only a limited amount of food (generally between three and six meals) and require a lot of cleanup and constant restocking.

For those who travel or already struggle to get everything done in a day, this is far from being a convenient or effective solution.

The Neakasa Riko Fresh-Made Wet Meal Feeder combines the health benefits of a wet-food diet with the convenience and high-capacity of a dry-food automatic feeder.

Unlike traditional automatic wet food feeders that can only store a handful of meals, the Neakasa Riko Fresh-Made Wet Meal Feeder can hold weeks of food at a time and dispense meals up to every hour, keeping kitties with even the most specialized dietary needs happy and hydrated throughout the day.

Rather than canned or wet packaged food, the Riko works with freeze-dried cat food. This shelf-stable food is ground up into portions, mixed with water, and allowed to rehydrate before serving.

No refrigeration or constant refilling needed. Just fill the hopper with a bag of freeze-dried food of your choice, add filtered water to the reservoir, set the amounts and feeding schedule on the app, and take a well-deserved break from fretting over your catâs meals and hydration status.

Neakasa is a smart-home and pet-care brand operated by Genhigh, a technology company headquartered in Shenzhen, China. Founded in 2017 as Neabot, the company specializes in automated solutions designed to make everyday home and pet care easier, including robotic cleaning and smart pet products. The Riko is manufactured in China, where the company is based.

Given the price point of this product, I wouldnât recommend it to cat owners simply hoping to unload some of their kitty chores to automation. There are less expensive automatic feeders for that. But for cat owners who normally feed wet food but are taking a long trip or frequently travel and want a feeder that can provide meals more often than their cat sitter can, the Riko Wet Meal Feeder is a worthwhile investment.

It is also a great option for cats who require small portions frequently throughout the day or who already eat freeze-dried food and can benefit from a more consistent schedule and more moisture in their diet.

Because this feeder allows for highly customized feeding routines and portions, it works well for kittens, adults, and seniors. But do be aware that the meal sizes cap out at 15g of dried food, which means larger cats may require multiple feedings throughout the day rather than the typical two meals they might be used to, something the app makes easy.

The Neakasa Riko takes the guesswork out of serving moistened meals. Simply fill the food hopper with compatible freeze-dried food, fill the water tank, and use the app to create a feeding schedule.

At mealtime, Riko automatically grinds the food, adds your selected amount of water, and allows the mixture to soak while the bowl is hidden out of reach. Once the food is ready, the bowl swings out so your cat can enjoy their fresh meal.

You can adjust the water-to-food ratio to create a consistency your cat prefers, from thicker to more soupy. Riko can schedule multiple meals throughout the day, add water to keep uneaten food fresh, and track food consumption through the app.

Beyond preparing moistened meals, the Riko packs several thoughtful features into the feeder itself:

Large capacity: The 3-liter food hopper and 2.4-liter water tank can hold enough for 10+ days of feeding.

Freshness-focused design: An airtight food compartment, desiccant system, and sealed grinder help protect freeze-dried food from moisture.

Precise portions: Riko weighs each serving for approximately Â±1-gram portioning.

Easy cleaning: The removable stainless-steel bowl is dishwasher-safe, while other components can be removed for cleaning. Each order comes with two bowls, so you can pop one in the dishwasher while the other is in use.

The Neakasa app gives you control over Riko from your phone, whether youâre home or away. You can create feeding schedules, adjust portion sizes and water-to-food ratios, and trigger extra meals remotely.

The app also records your catâs food and water intake, making it easier to spotchanges in eating habits over time. Youâll receive alerts for low food and water storage and potential feeding problems, while adjustable settings let you configure features such as freshness detection, child lock, and desiccant replacement reminders.

Through the app, you have control over the amount of ground food in each meal, the ratio of water added, how long it sits to rehydrate, and how often water is added if food is left over. You can even program âwater onlyâ meals to encourage even more moisture intake.

Riko can be customized with a few optional accessories. The rechargeable battery pack provides up to seven days of cordless operation and backup power during outages, while the Multi-Cat Access Module uses microchip recognition to restrict feeding to each designated cat in multi-cat households.

Neakasa also sells replacement silicone desiccant packs with a color-changing indicator that lets you know when the pack needs replacing.

Number of meals per fill: about 10 daysâ worth

Compatible with: most types of freeze-dried food

Number of meals per fill: 3 daysâ worth

Compatible with: all types of canned food

If youâve read any of my reviews before, then you know that my cat, Makoa, is a BIG fan of food. So any device that makes meal times less of a hassle for me and more accessible for him is worth trying out. And, since our family also travels fairly frequently, I thought this high-tech contraption might be helpful in multiple ways.

When the Riko arrived, I immediately felt like I was unboxing some kind of fancy kitty espresso maker! Itâs about the same size as one, and the grinder really does look very similar to a coffee grinder.

Getting the Riko set up was fairly painless. I followed the Quick Start Instructions to assemble the few parts that had been stored internally during shipping, then downloaded the app and connected the device to my Wi-Fi.

From there, things got a touch trickier. Because the Riko works using weight, not volume, it can be a little difficult to set the proportions for each meal. For example, I typically feed Makoa Â¼ cup twice per day. How many grams of ground freeze-dried food plus water is that? No idea.

Luckily, the app does have a very helpful Smart Feeding Plan setup that allows you to use your catâs weight and select the type of food you feed to automatically create a feeding schedule based on the food brand's recommended intake.

The downside here is that it defaults to 10 meals per day. Which probably isnât a bad thing since cats did evolve to eat multiple small meals throughout the day (and this also guarantees better hydration). But if your cat is used to a couple of big meals at the same time each day, this can make for a tough transition.

I ended up manually adding up the dry food total it recommended, then manually adding meals that were more aligned with his typical schedule.

The other hangup I ran into is that the feeder (in the US, at least) maxes out at 15g of ground food per meal. For comparison, my 12-pound cat needs about 60g of ground food per day. In other words, I had to schedule at least four meals per day for him to get all the food he needs.

These smaller meal sizes are intentional. Not only does it help avoid food being wasted (or left out for too long without being eaten), but it also ensures your cat is continually taking in food-based moisture throughout the dayâthe way they evolved to.

So I wouldnât say this is a bad thing or design flaw, but it is something you and your cat may need to adjust to.

Beyond the tricky parts of portioning and scheduling, I really do love this feeder! It is so easy to fill and, once the schedule is set, you really can just forget it. It starts preparing each meal ahead of time so that the food is ready at the scheduled mealtime.

It makes a recognizable beep when food is ready, so your cat can learn to come as soon as dinner is served. (Makoa learned to recognize the low buzz of the grinder almost instantly, and now waits for his meals twenty minutes before they are served.)

Not only has this gadget taken the stress off me (now Makoa has something else to obsess over when itâs dinner time), but it has made it so much easier to ensure consistent, moist meals throughout the day. And I know it will be a lifesaver for those weekend trips and long vacations our family likes to go on.

I highly recommend this feeder to anyone who is looking for a way to automate their catâs meals without having to rely on dry kibble. The rehydrated freeze-dried food isnât the same as canned food, but the texture is similar, and most cats love this type of food, especially when it is mixed with water. Even better, freeze-dried food tends to be healthier and more nutrient-dense than even the best canned food options.

No. Riko is designed to grind and rehydrate freeze-dried food, not conventional wet food. Do not put canned, pouch, or other wet food, or kibble, dehydrated, or air-dried food into the hopper.

Riko's smart features and remote app controls require a Wi-Fi connection, but once programmed, the feeder can still perform its feeding schedule if the internet connection is interrupted. It supports 2.4 GHz Wi-Fi networks.

Because Riko adds water to the food before serving, the resulting meal should be treated like wet food. Neakasa recommends that your cat consume it within about three to four hours.

Riko's freshness settings can detect leftover food and pause the next scheduled feeding when the amount remaining exceeds your chosen threshold. The feeder can also retract the bowl after food has remained uneaten for an extended period.

If hydration is a concern for your cat and providing consistent moist food is a challenge for you, then the Neakasa Riko is worth looking into.

This high-tech automatic feeder can store 10 days' worth of freeze-dried food at a time and provide up to 20 freshly rehydrated meals per day. Each meal can be scheduled and proportioned to meet your catâs needs while ensuring their moisture intake is optimal to avoid future health issues. It's perfect for busy cat parents, extended periods away, and cats who require frequent, moistened meals.

Forget traditional Christmas tree decorations! Sarah Jessica Parker's pretty alternative is as gorgeous as it is affordable.

When you purchase through links on our site, we may earn an affiliate commission. Here’s how it works.

Thanks to her stint in The Family Stone, Sarah Jessica Parker's name has long been synonymous with the holidays for fans – and even more so now she's shared her Christmas tree trick with us all!

Yes, it is now possible to give your Christmas tree that Carrie Bradshaw stamp of approval! And, somewhat gloriously, SJP's approach to festive decor has the same sort of wonderfully unfussy vibe as Michelle Obama's twig tree, which means you don't need a celebrity-sized budget to recreate the look. In fact, all you really need is baby's breath.

This underrated flower has spent most of its life being a supporting actor to bigger and better roses, or a wispy filler flower tucked into grocery store bouquets. But when Kristin Davis posted an Instagram video of herself arranging flowers blindfolded (as one does), Sarah Jessica Parker left a surprising comment: “You can use babies breath in your Christmas tree.” Say what?

Now, Kristin Davis (who worked at a florist in college) wasn’t keen on using it for her own tree (very Charlotte-coded), but she did share a rule worth stealing: if you're going to do it, then always arrange flowers in odd numbers, like three or five.

For me, though, SJP’s comment about using baby’s breath in her Christmas tree has set my imagination alight! And with that in mind, I asked some experts how I could use them in my own holiday decoration this year.

The biggest risk when it comes to stealing Sarah Jessica Parker's idea is overdoing it. Roberta Sabbatini, founder of ItalianTouch Events, says, “The main mistake is using too much. The beauty of baby’s breath is its lightness.” Morgan Brooks of Plant Style Home puts it even better, saying, “One loose spiral is elegant. Three is a snowstorm, and the tree disappears behind it.”

Sign up for the Gardening Know How newsletter today and receive a free copy of our e-book "How to Grow Delicious Tomatoes".

Remember that odd-number rule? CEO of Florals Memories Nadi Melam clips her baby’s breath into “clouds” and adds them in threes, noting, “Baby’s breath looks beautiful on trees because of negative space.” Translation: let the tree breathe!

For a spiral, Brooks gathers five to seven stems, wires each bunch at the base, and tucks the ends deep into the branches. Sabbatini also skips pushing loose stems into the tree and instead secures each little bundle with florist wire or ribbon.

Fresh baby’s breath is a diva out of water. Brooks says fresh stems “wilt within a day or two indoors,” while dried versions keep their shape all season and can be packed away for next year. Melam agrees that dried is “far easier to work with.” If you do love fresh, just be sure to add it on Christmas Eve.

If you don't have time for the drying process, this Bexikou dried baby’s breath bouquet comes ready to use, and its short white stems are well suited to wiring into small, airy clusters for your tree.

Drying your own for a Sarah Jessica Parker-style tree is simple. Bundle five to seven stems with twine, hang them upside down in a dark, warm, well-ventilated room, and check after five days, as outlined in our guide to growing baby’s breath. If you’re short on time, ready-dried bunches work just as well.

On an artificial tree, Brooks adds fine floral wire around the branch wire, since the stems are too light to stay put when someone brushes past.

Warm white lights, clear glass ornaments, and velvet ribbon are baby’s breath’s best friends. Brooks adds pearl baubles and silver or soft gold ribbon to the list, but warns that rustic burlap and heavy red ornaments “fight it.” Treat baby’s breath as one of just two or three ideas on the tree, not the whole script.

Pair your baby’s breath with a strand of Northlight 100-count warm white LED mini lights, which stay cool to the touch and give the soft, candlelit glow that suits a delicate white filler.

Dried stems are brittle and, as Melam notes, highly flammable. Use cool LED lights and keep bunches away from hot bulbs and open flames. Baby’s breath is also mildly toxic to cats, so if pets are around, keep it to the upper two-thirds of the tree and sweep up anything that falls.

Baby’s breath is easy to grow, so sow seeds next spring, cut and dry the blooms in summer, and next December’s tree is sorted. Will your tree look like a Manhattan brownstone from a certain Sarah Jessica Parker-fronted TV series? Possibly, but only if you resist the urge to add a fourth bunch.

#8045. How To Give Medicine To A Child Who Refuses: Tips For Sensitive Kids

A pediatrician and a nurse practitioner share how to get medicine, saline, and bandages past kids who’d rather do anything else, plus how to handle the guilt afterward.

Has your child ever run around the house to avoid having their scraped-up knee cleaned and bandaged? Does a dose of antibiotics require two adults, one to immobilize and one to administer the medication? And potentially a change of clothing for you and/or your child afterwards? If so, you might have a sensitive sick kid.

All kids are miserable when they are sick, but for children who are neurodivergent, have disabilities, and/or sensory sensitivities, symptoms can feel more intense and be more challenging to manage. And it always seems that the kids who struggle the most are the ones who will inevitably catch every bug. Unfortunately, my family is a regular fixture at our pediatrician’s office and our local CVS pharmacy as a result.

Medication administration is not easy for a lot of parents. And during illnesses such as the flu, strep throat, or ear infections, a whole host of medications may be recommended for pain, fever reduction, or coughs. While some of these medications are available in “kid-friendly” flavors, it doesn’t mean that your sensitive kiddo is going to agree with that assessment. Board-certified pediatrician Dr. Lauren Hughes recommends that parents choose their battles, because many medications, while helpful in ideal circumstances, aren’t critical for recovery.

“There is no real good data for vapor rubs or OTC cough meds in kids under 6 years. Honestly, my favorite cough medicine [for] children is just a spoonful of honey,” says Hughes. “When it comes to things like ibuprofen and acetaminophen, these are helpful for controlling pain and discomfort, which can often help the child feel better so they will continue drinking and staying hydrated. However, a fever itself is not harmful in children over 60 days with normal immune systems.”

Lindsay McHugh, DNP, a board-certified psychiatric mental health nurse practitioner and co-founder of Resting Roo, recommends that parents of children who have difficulty taking medications experiment with other ways to ease symptoms. “You [can] try heating packs to alleviate pain or ice packs, or if they have a stuffy, you could warm that up in the microwave, and they could hold it on a certain spot,” McHugh says, “[For fever] a warm bath or a lukewarm or even a cool bath, whatever feels right to your child at the time… to make them as comfortable as possible.”

Both McHugh and Hughes say taking the full course of antibiotics if prescribed needs to be parents’ priority. “If we don’t take [all] the antibiotics, then they could potentially build a resistance,” says McHugh. “If they build a resistance, then we have even sicker kids for even longer.”

Unfortunately, antibiotics — which can taste disgusting and/or have gritty textures — can be the biggest medication battle. Hughes has the following recommendations:

An absolute game changer in our family has been my daughter learning to swallow pills. Now I wish we had tried it much sooner. McHugh says that while some 3-year-olds might be ready, parents usually can start trying with their children at age 4 or 5. “[You can start] practicing with certain foods that are somewhat pill-shaped, not too big, something soft… like a pea,” says McHugh, “[And say], ‘Let’s practice trying to not chew your pea. Let’s practice trying to swallow it.’ Practice outside of being sick. So then when they are sick, then it’s not so foreign.”

Once my daughter got the hang of it, it changed everything: When she needed antibiotics a couple months later, the pediatrician was able to prescribe pills she could swallow.

Our entire family has a history of sensitive skin, allergies, and skin ailments like eczema. These seem to frequently coexist in individuals with other sensory sensitivities. Both my daughter and I, for example, can react to the adhesive in some Band-Aids. Now we use Band-Aids for Sensitive Skin for her or, alternatively, sensitive skin tape and non-stick gauze for protecting and healing cuts and injuries.

While it’s ideal to only use products that you know your child likes and doesn’t react to, sometimes you need to make a change or try something new for a symptom or illness you haven’t encountered before. For items with topical application, McHugh recommends checking out Environmental Working Group’s Skin Deep database to research products that may include ingredients you know your child is allergic or sensitive to or might cause a reaction.

McHugh recommends trying out new topical items on an area of the body where your child is the least sensitive (which will be different for every child), while they are healthy. “Pick a 1x1 or a 2x2 inch square, and try the product, a little bit at a time. I would…see how they [and] how their skin responds,” says McHugh, “So maybe on day two or three we do this whole leg [and] see if that’s not too overwhelming from skin sensitivity as well as the smell or feel.”

Since my daughter and I are both sensitive to smells, I also have her smell-test products in the store aisle before we buy.

Since I have a kiddo who is sensitive to touch and texture even when she is feeling 100%, standard oral thermometers have pretty much been a no-go since she was an infant, and temporal thermometers can be tricky on a sweaty kid who doesn’t like to be touched. A no-touch forehead thermometer gets a quick read without any contact, and one with a silent mode lets you take overnight temps without waking them.

Illness can be especially tricky for younger children who can’t (or won’t) blow their noses. But Hughes says it is especially critical for infants who are under six months who are still exclusively breast- or bottle-fed: When they’re congested, they can’t breathe while feeding and are likely to become dehydrated.

For using inhalers, nasal aspirators, and nasal saline, Hughes recommends the following hold: “The adult sits down with their legs spread in a V. They put the child’s head up between their legs and then place the child’s arms under their thighs. The parent then crosses their shins/ankles over the child’s legs to hold them in place. This allows the parent to have both hands free while the child is immobilized without harming them.”

Here are some other tips for treatment of congestion, drainage, and coughs:

Illnesses and injuries can be exhausting for sensitive kids and their parents. And it can be easy to start feeling guilty for having to force your child to take medicine or do some other treatment that was uncomfortable, even if it was best for them and helped them feel better in the long term. This can be especially challenging if you are trying to teach your children about bodily autonomy and boundaries.

McHugh recommends that parents try to be clear before these moments about what you are going to have to do, that you are taking care of them, they are safe, and that you know that it may be uncomfortable, painful, or taste yucky.

“[After] I would offer empathy [and] validate their experience,” says McHugh, “And then I would say, ‘I know in the past we've talked about body autonomy, body safety. And it feels like Mommy and Daddy broke that. I’m sorry that we did that… However, we have to take care of you, and your safety is our number one priority.’”

When our kids are sick or have an injury, it’s a high-stress time. You’re worried about your child, but you’re also worried about doing the right thing and taking care of them the right way. And sometimes you need to do what you need to do, whether it is accepting help from those around you, asking for a break, or yes, bribing your child to cooperate with some part of their care.

“When your child isn’t feeling good, you’re already on edge. It’s most appropriate to treat [them] so that they don’t get sicker, and we want to take care of our babies and do everything we can. And if it takes a couple extra popsicles…that’s perfectly okay,” reflects McHugh, “Don’t forget to take care of yourself; it’s the last thing on the list. But [sometimes] you just need a little break to go to the bathroom and cry, because it was awful.”

#8044. 48 Bulldogs, One Apartment, and a Disturbing Secret

We just sent a welcome email your way with a quick overview of what to expect (including those vital recall alerts).

This is exactly why we are against puppy mills.

Forty-eight dogs â mostly French Bulldogs and English Bulldogs â found in what authorities are describing as a clandestine breeding operation in San Juan de Miraflores, Peru.

And when you read what was found, it is hard not to feel angry.

Authorities discovered the animals in appalling conditions on September 28 in an apartment on JirÃ³n Santiago RodrÃ­guez. The group included 25 French Bulldogs, nine English Bulldogs, eight mixed-breed dogs, five French Bulldog puppies, and one Dachshund. There was also a rooster. Local French Bulldog club, Club Frenchie, heard about the rescue through social media and immediately reached out to offer assistance. One member of the club spoke to a reporter from the Peruvian newspaper El Comercio about what they had witnessed:

âThe state of health was absolutely deplorable. There were dogs covered in feces, filthy, with no hygiene whatsoever, dogs with broken nails, bitten ears, and other serious problems,â he said.

The dogs were brought to the Municipal Veterinary Clinic in San Juan de Miraflores, where they were examined and received treatment for a range of conditions. Most were suffering from heat stress, and many had excessively long nails, some bleeding, skin problems, fungal issues, eye infections, surgical scars, and other conditions requiring medical attention. Six puppies reportedly needed incubator care, with two described as being in a particularly fragile condition.

Following the intervention, the animals were taken to the municipal veterinary service, and some have since been moved into foster care. The San Juan de Miraflores Provincial Corporate Criminal Prosecutor's Office is investigating the case, and FÃ©lix Sonco and Darlys Vanegas were arrested at the scene.

As if the horrendous conditions that greeted rescuers werenât disturbing enough, it appears that this wasnât simply a breeding operation, but an illegal, makeshift veterinary clinic.

Some of these dogs had undergone surgery on their vocal cords; a barbaric procedure known as debarking. Being kept in cramped and filthy conditions meant that these dogs were barking and crying constantly. Debarking was a way to reduce noise and avoid complaints.

They didnât improve conditions. They didnât provide relief. They simply removed their ability to voice their distress.

Evidence also suggests that several female Bulldogs were bred repeatedly, with some reportedly forced to carry as many as ten litters of puppies. Veterinary examination also found evidence that crude cesarean surgeries had been performed prematurely to get puppies out faster and back on the market, while the mothers, if they survived, were bred again.

Investigators reportedly found premature newborn puppies inside an unsterilized incubator, while puppies were being sold for around 1,500 to 2,500 Peruvian soles each â roughly $400 to $670 USD.

French Bulldogs and English Bulldogs are brachycephalic breeds. Their shortened skull and squishy faces are a big part of their appeal. But there is a very uncomfortable truth behind that cute face.

That same anatomy that many people find irresistible can make it harder for a dog to breathe, exercise, sleep, regulate their body temperature, and, in some cases, give birth.

We have to stop pretending these things are simply âpart of being a Bulldog.â

A dog struggling to breathe is not just a snorer. A dog that overheats easily is not just âsensitive to the heat.â These are medical problems.

Brachycephalic obstructive airway syndrome (BOAS) refers to the conditions that affect breeds with a shortened skull, or âbrachycephaly.â These conditions include hypoplastic trachea (narrow  windpipe), stenotic nares (narrow nostrils), and a tongue and soft palate that are too large and long for the mouth, resulting in obstruction of the airways and difficulty swallowing.

These issues have led many veterinary professionals and animal welfare advocates to question the ethics of breeding these dogs. When a physical characteristic can affect basic functions like breathing and temperature regulation, choosing which dogs reproduce needs to consider more than appearance.

That little flat face. Those big eyes. The stout little body. The funny little snorts.

Most people see cute, even adorable. But as veterinarians, we see a whole list of problems that need to be monitored.

A Bulldog can be an absolutely wonderful companion and still have anatomy that puts them at risk for serious health problems. Breeding of these dogs should require more responsibility, not less, with breeders selecting for less extreme conformations.

There is something very sad about how much importance we place on how dogs look. A certain face. A certain size. A certain coat. A certain breed.

The more desirable that look becomes, the more money there is in producing it. That creates a market, and unfortunately, where there is money, there will always be those willing to cut corners.

This does not mean that every breeder is bad. There are responsible breeders who health-test their dogs, carefully select breeding pairs, provide appropriate veterinary care, and take responsibility for the puppies they bring into the world. Those who are actively trying to breed healthier versions of dogs whose health and function have been crippled through selective breeding for exaggerated features.

Puppy mills are something very different.

The problem is when the animals producing those puppies become a means to an end.

And veterinary care becomes an expense to minimize or avoid, not an essential part of responsible animal care.

When it comes to looking for your next four-legged family member, start your search at an animal shelter. Research your favorite breed and know how to recognize a suspicious situation.

If you are planning to purchase or adopt a puppy, you should be able to inspect the home or facility where the puppy was raised, and meet the puppyâs mother. Breeders who are unwilling or unable to allow this raise suspicions of unethical practice, and if you are concerned about a potential welfare issue, donât be tempted to buy a puppy to ârescueâ it â this simply finances the operation. Instead, contact your local animal control agency, humane society, sheriff, or police department.

When extreme conformation interferes with breathing and thermoregulation, when it increases the risk of difficult births and chronic airway problems, we need to consider whether breeding these dogs is the right thing to do. But if people will buy them, people will breed them.

Itâs up to us to look past the adorable face we saw on Instagram and ask:

And, as the horrific plight of these 48 dogs reminds us, where did they come from?

The problem is loving an appearance so much that we stop asking what that appearance means for the animal.

These dogs have been through a terrible situation, but now they have a chance.

They need veterinary care. Their nails need treatment, their skin and eyes need evaluation, their nutritional needs need to be addressed, and their other medical problems need to be properly investigated. Some require specialized treatment, while others are recovering in foster homes.

And hopefully, many of these dogs will eventually experience something that should have been completely ordinary from the beginning:

These dogs were not born to produce puppies. They were not born to be quiet. They were not born to look a certain way for someone else's profit.

For that reason, adoption should always be considered before buying a puppy.

There are so many wonderful dogs already waiting in shelters, foster homes, and recovering from neglect. Dogs that may not have the perfect face or pedigree but have an enormous capacity to love.

Please, before asking where to buy the puppy with the cutest face, ask who is already waiting for someone to choose them.

#8043. Your kid needs you to have hobbies outside of motherhood. Here’s why

Hobbies aren’t a luxury for moms. They boost well-being, nurture identity, and show our children what a full life looks like.

By Lauren Ramakrishna Updated Nov. 13, 2026

Twenty-four years. That’s how long it had been since I last stood atop a swim block, preparing to dive in for a timed race in an official meet.

A whistle blew. The crowd hushed to silence. A monotone call came over the loudspeaker, “Swimmers, take your mark,” followed by a loud electronic beep that signaled the start of the race. I felt the cold rush of water overtake my body upon diving in. The neurons in my brain feverishly told my muscles to complete the strokes I’d learned decades before. In seconds, it was done. I finished the race.

When I got out of the pool, I walked over to my kids. My son, a competitive swimmer himself, looked at me and earnestly said, “Wow, Mom. I’m proud of you.”

Like most moms, I have a packed schedule. I work, parent, volunteer at school, shepherd my two kids to practices and social gatherings, throw meals together, walk the dog, and occasionally find a moment to breathe. But over the past couple of years, I watched my growing kids, now ages 12 and 9, discover and engage in passions that light them up. It left me wondering, why not me, too?

“A recurring theme in my practice is women feeling they’ve lost their individual identities somewhere between work, parenting, and meeting everyone else’s needs,” says Carly Snyder, a New York City–based reproductive and perinatal psychiatrist. “Part of my work involves helping women recognize that their own interests and needs are legitimate.”

In an effort to start prioritizing my own interests, I jumped at the chance to sign up for a summer swim league for adults aptly named “Grown-Up Swimming.” The whole experience reignited my love for swimming, and it showed me and my kids that I’m more than just a mom.

Research highlights a multitude of benefits earned by pursuing hobbies. Hobbyists often have wider social networks, improved mental health markers, and enhanced positive emotions.

Hobbies offer a particularly important lifeline for mothers, who often report losing themselves to the demanding needs of family life. That rings true for Kaitlyn Edington, an art educator and mom of two who recalls struggling after returning to work as a teacher following the birth of her first child. “I was so depleted,” Edington says. She spent her workdays teaching with short breaks to pump, often bringing her computer into her pumping room so she could catch up on work, then went home to full nights of infant care.

One day while scrolling on Instagram, Edington saw an artist posting images of her sketchbook paintings. “She changed my life,” Edington says. “Her sketchbook paintings were so loose and free, and she was encouraging people to draw everyday. I remember thinking, ‘If I have to pump two to three times a day, which I absolutely hate, why not pair it with something that I love?’” From then on, Edington sketched when she pumped, and ultimately developed a habit of daily sketching that she continues 10 years later.

No longer in the pumping phase of life, Edington ensures she gets time to sketch by waking up before her kids. “I hold the habit of waking up before my kids as sacred,” she says. “I need that time, when nobody needs me. It’s my emotional rest.”

Science backs Edington’s belief that her hobby stabilizes her mental health. “Reengaging in meaningful, enjoyable activities can be therapeutically valuable,” Snyder says. “Behavioral activation, an evidence-based treatment for depression, specifically emphasizes reconnecting with activities that provide pleasure, purpose, or a sense of accomplishment.”

Snyder has three children, ages 19, 16, and 11, and throughout their lives she has maintained her dedication to skiing, cycling, yoga and running, completing a total of 19 marathons. She knows her kids benefit from her hobbies. Each time Snyder trains for an upcoming marathon, “[My kids] witness my commitment, discipline, setbacks, and perseverance,” she says. “Watching a parent pursue a hobby provides opportunities to observe persistence, emotional regulation, problem-solving, and enjoyment.”

But those benefits are secondary to the impacts hobbies have on the women pursuing them. “I think we’ve become so accustomed to framing everything mothers do in terms of how it benefits their children,” Snyder says. “Women are entitled to happiness and fulfillment for their own sake.”

It’s simply an added bonus that when mom is happy for mom’s sake, the benefits for her kids naturally follow, according to multiple studies linking a mother’s well-being with her child’s. Plus, kids also learn that all stages of adulthood, including those under the umbrella of parenting, can include personal fulfillment, curiosity, and growth.

The best way to start a hobby is to let yourself reconnect with something you already love. I remembered how much joy I got out of competing in swim meets in high school, and I was eager to recreate that glee. Ask yourself, “What did I love when I was a kid or a young adult?”

Your hobby doesn’t have to involve intense commitment. “Reading, gardening, dancing, listening to music, or simply spending time alone can be just as meaningful as running a marathon,” Snyder says.

Search online for local groups involved in the activity you want to pursue. Your local library may have resources to help you get started as well.

When you’re ready to commit, set realistic goals. Start by focusing on your hobby consistently for just 10-15 minutes per day. Showing up is the main goal.

“Motherhood should expand a woman’s identity, not erase it,” Snyder advises. Which hobby will help expand yours?

Ever since we started inviting cats into our homes, humans have been looking for better ways to deal with the unavoidable issue of their waste. Cats are fastidiously clean by nature, and teaching them to use a litter box is usually pretty straightforward. Keeping that litter box clean is decidedly more labor-intensive.

Maintaining good litter box hygiene isnât just about controlling odors. Some cats will happily share a litter box, while others will refuse to use soiled litter, even if they are the only cat using it. Inappropriate toileting â that is, peeing or pooping in shoes, on bedding, in fruit bowls(!) â can be a sign of a health problem, but more often than not, itâs about the litter box itself. The wrong location, the wrong type of litter, and most significantly, a box that isnât clean.

And if, like me, you have more than one feline in the family, youâve likely got multiple litter boxes that you spend an immeasurable amount of time scooping, sifting, and cleaning.

But now I realize how much it has also improved the lives of my cats. Instead of having to wait for me to provide them with a fresh tray, the automatic cleaning function means every cat gets a clean litter box for every visit.

Not having to scoop out litter boxes every day has been a total game-changer for me, and while itâs hard to put a price on how much my catsâ quality of life has improved, itâs nice to know that, at less than $150, the PetPivot Autoscooper 12 is well within reach of most pet owners.

The Autoscooper 12 is the newest self-cleaning litter box from PetPivot. The US company was founded in Portland, Oregon, in 2023. Following the overwhelming success of the AutoScooper 11, PetPivot released the new model in 2026, which is available in the US, Europe, the United Kingdom, Canada, Japan, and Australia.

The AutoScooper 12 is a quieter, more compact unit that features upgraded motion sensors for improved safety and accuracy, and an integrated step that provides easier access for smaller cats or those with mobility issues.

If youâre worried that an open litter box means more litter tracking and unpleasant odors, donât be. The deep placement of the tray and the odor-locking design of the waste drawer minimizes litter scatter and keeps bad smells well-contained.

The litter tray contains a removable mat made from durable, water-resistant 300D Oxford fabric that minimizes âlitter stickâ and makes cleaning a breeze. For the most part, routine cleaning of the AutoScooper 12 consists of emptying the waste drawer once or twice a week (depending on the number of cats using it) and brushing any stray litter from around the unit. No more daily scooping. You will occasionally need to give the whole unit a proper clean, but itâs a relatively painless process.

Compared with the previous model, the AutoScooper 12 takes up less floor space, but also has a slightly smaller tray, which some particularly large or messy cats may struggle with. However, the open design provides most cats with plenty of room to move, and with an operating volume of 32 dB, itâs perfect for smaller spaces and apartment living.

In terms of function and design, the AutoScooper 12 is up there with the best, at a fraction of the price. Plus, it comes in a range of different colors, including pink!
